Description 99.1 Pharming presents positive Phase II topline data for leniolisib in genetic PIDs with immune dysregulation at ESID 2026 SIGNATURE Pursuant to the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the registrant has duly caused this report to be signed on its behalf by the undersigned, thereunto duly authorized.

By: /s/ Kenneth Lynard Name: Kenneth Lynard Title: Interim Co-CEO & CFO Date: October 14, 2026 Pharming p resents positive Phase II topline data for leniolisib in genetic PIDs with immune dysregulation at ESID 2026 • First clinical data for leniolisib in a larger group of PID participants beyond APDS, supporting the potential of targeted PI3Kδ inhibition to address immune dysregulation • Leniolisib was well-tolerated, with benefits observed across multiple measures of immune dysregulation, including improvement in lymphoproliferation and positive trends in lung and liver disease markers • All participants who completed the study elected to continue receiving treatment in a long-term extension study Leiden, the Netherlands, October 14, 2026: Pharming (Euronext Amsterdam: PHARM/Nasdaq: PHAR), a global biotechnology company focused on rare immune and genetic diseases, today presented positive topline data from its Phase II trial of leniolisib in genetically identifiable primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs) with immune dysregulation linked to altered PI3Kδ signaling.

We look forward to reporting topline results from our separate Phase II trial in CVID, expected in November, which will inform our plans for a potential registrational study in the broader CVID population.” Based on estimated prevalence rates, these genetically identifiable PIDs and CVID with immune dysregulation represent a broader potential patient population than APDS, with estimated prevalence of approximately 7.5 patients per million for genetic PIDs and approximately 39 patients per million for CVID, including overlap between the genetic PID and CVID populations, compared with approximately 1.5 patients per million for APDS.
